Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa for tourism in Belgium, applied for in advance. The Belgian mission in India says the application form is completed online and then submitted in person at the VFS Visa Application Centre (New Delhi embassy VAC for North and East India, Mumbai consulate VAC for West and South India); the online form is valid for 30 days, after which it is deleted if you have not attended the VAC. Travel insurance of at least EUR 30,000 covering all risks for the whole trip, including the days of arrival and departure, is required and the policy must be signed by the applicant (the mission links an approved-insurer list). A short stay is up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Passport validity of at least 3 months after departure, issued within the previous 10 years, is the Schengen rule stated on Belgium's foreign ministry exemption page. Belgium also requires every short-stay visitor to declare their presence within three days of arriving; since 10 April 2026 this can be done online through the 'My address in Belgium' form (Belgian foreign ministry pages). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (official ETIAS website says it is not in operation). The mission's page gives no processing time, so none is stated here.
fee_notes: Short-stay (C) handling fee EUR 90 (children 6 to 12: EUR 45; under 6 free), paid in Indian rupees at the exchange rate communicated by the Belgian embassy in New Delhi and non-refundable. A separate VAC service fee of INR 2,750 (inclusive of taxes) is charged even to applicants exempt from the visa fee. Amounts are subject to change (Belgian mission in India page).

conditions_text: No visa needed for short stays in Belgium (Schengen area) of up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined (Belgian embassy in the US: US citizens do not require a C-visa). A stay over 90 days needs a Belgian long-stay (D) visa. Visa exemption does not waive the Schengen entry conditions: passport valid at least 3 months after you leave and issued within the previous 10 years, a stated purpose of travel and sufficient means (Belgian foreign ministry exemption guidance). The EU Entry/Exit System registers non-EU travellers (photo, fingerprints) at the Schengen external border. Belgium also requires every short-stay visitor to declare their presence within three days of arriving; since 10 April 2026 this can be done online through the 'My address in Belgium' form (Belgian foreign ministry pages). Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now; check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change. Note: the Belgian embassy's US page (last updated 3 September 2025) says ETIAS will start in the last quarter of 2026, but the official ETIAS website currently gives no start date.

UK citizens with a full British passport can visit Belgium without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the Schengen area (UK FCDO entry requirements for Belgium, used as the source because Belgium's own UK-embassy page predates current rules). Passport must have been issued less than 10 years before arrival and be valid at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area. At the Belgian border you may be asked for a return or onward ticket and proof of enough money for your stay. EES registration (photo, fingerprints) applies at the border. Other UK travel documents (for example blue or red travel documents) may need a visa. Belgium also requires every short-stay visitor to declare their presence within three days of arriving; since 10 April 2026 this can be done online through the 'My address in Belgium' form (Belgian foreign ministry pages). UK citizens are covered by ETIAS once it starts; the UK ETA is a separate scheme for people entering the UK and does not apply here.

The Canada eTA is a separate scheme for entering Canada and does not apply here.

Australian citizens do not need a visa to travel to Belgium for business or personal travel; the stay in the Schengen area should not exceed 90 days in a 6-month (180-day) period (Belgian embassy in Australia). Passport must be valid for at least 3 months on the day you leave Belgium (embassy page); the Schengen rule also requires it to have been issued within the previous 10 years (Belgian foreign ministry exemption guidance). The EU Entry/Exit System registers non-EU travellers (photo, fingerprints) at the Schengen external border. Belgium also requires every short-stay visitor to declare their presence within three days of arriving; since 10 April 2026 this can be done online through the 'My address in Belgium' form (Belgian foreign ministry pages). The Australian ETA is a separate scheme for entering Australia and does not apply here.

EU freedom of movement: German citizens can enter and travel in Belgium with either a valid passport or a valid national identity card (the document must be valid on the day of travel). No visa, no ETIAS and no EES registration apply to EU citizens. The 90-day limit for non-EU visitors does not apply to EU citizens; the EU's Your Europe site lists registering your presence after the first 3 months as a separate residence formality, not an entry visa.

Singapore citizens are exempt from applying for the Schengen short-stay visa and may stay in the Schengen zone for a maximum of 90 days in each period of 180 days (Belgian embassy in Singapore). Visa exemption does not waive the Schengen entry conditions: passport valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years, a stated purpose of stay and sufficient means of subsistence (Belgian foreign ministry exemption guidance). Brazilian citizens do not need a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period in Belgium and the rest of the Schengen area (Belgian embassy page in Portuguese, updated 8 October 2026). The stay cannot be extended beyond 90 days in any 180 days. The passport must be valid for at least 3 months. The page also states the traveller should have at least EUR 95 per day available for expenses and says travel insurance with at least EUR 30,000 cover is mandatory for entry to the Schengen area; carry both proofs. Belgium also requires every short-stay visitor to declare their presence within three days of arriving; since 10 April 2026 this can be done online through the 'My address in Belgium' form (Belgian foreign ministry pages). ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, EUR 20) is NOT in force today (the Belgian embassy page agrees: ETIAS is not yet operational): the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked 19 October 2026) says it is currently not in operation, no applications are being collected, and the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now; check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change. Belgium has no direct flights from Brazil, so the embassy advises checking the entry conditions of the first Schengen country on your ticket.

Indian ordinary-passport holders can visit Hong Kong visa-free for up to 14 days, but only after successfully completing the Immigration Department's online Pre-arrival Registration (PAR), which is in force today and required before travel. PAR needs an Indian passport valid for at least six months. A registration lasts six months and allows multiple visits of up to 14 days each; renewing or replacing the passport requires a new registration, and the same passport must be used for travel. At the airport you must present both the signed PAR notification slip and the same Indian passport; presenting only one can lead to refused boarding or refused entry, and holding the slip does not guarantee entry. PAR is not needed by holders of a valid Hong Kong entry visa, a valid HKSAR Travel Pass, enrolled e-Channel frequent-visitor members, Indian nationals with the right of abode or right to land or valid permission to remain for employment, study or residence in Hong Kong, or Indian diplomatic/official passport holders; direct air transit that stays in the airport transit area also needs no PAR. These concessions relate to Hong Kong documents, not to visas of other countries, so no foreign-visa cascade applies. Stays over 14 days or for any other purpose need a visa applied for directly with the Hong Kong Immigration Department. Hong Kong is a Special Administrative Region of China with its own entry rules, separate from mainland China. The Immigration Department also states that visitors must have adequate funds for their stay without working and, unless in transit to the Chinese Mainland or Macao, hold onward or return tickets. Entry is still subject to immigration control.
fee_notes: PAR is free of charge. The Immigration Department says it has not authorised any agent or website to handle PAR; use only the official government service.

conditions_text: Indian passport holders need a Cuban tourist visa before travel; Cuba's embassy page for India lists the tourist visa (tourist card) as single-entry, for tourism only, with the passport, a form and a plane ticket showing arrival and return dates as documents. Cuba's tourist-visa system: Cuban consular pages say the paper tourist card (tarjeta del turista) has been joined by an electronic tourist visa issued at evisacuba.cu; a Cuban Ministry of Tourism announcement carried on a Cuban embassy site (22 Jan 2025) says that from 30 June 2025 every tourist entering Cuba must hold the electronic visa. You apply online, receive a 10-character code by email, and enter it into the D'Viajeros entry form (dviajeros.mitrans.gob.cu), which then emails you a QR code to show on arrival (print it too, as wifi may be poor). Sources differ on how early to complete D'Viajeros: the Cuban tourism ministry said within 7 days before the trip (Jan 2025), Canada and Singapore say up to 72 hours before arrival, Germany says within 48 hours before check-in; do it as the airline requires. A Cuban embassy page for online tourist visas gives a single entry valid for 90 days, extendable (Cuba's mission in Trinidad and Tobago); older Cuban embassy pages still describe the tourist card as 30 days plus a 30-day extension. That embassy page's own wording is 30 days plus a 30-day extension; I did not find an India-specific page that states 90 days, so max_stay_days is left null. Passport must have at least 6 months' validity (Cuban consular guidance). Carry an onward or return ticket. Medical insurance valid for Cuba is expected: be ready to show proof on arrival, Canada and Germany say Cuban cover can be bought at the port of entry if you have none. Check the latest on whether airlines still fly to Cuba: several have cut flights because of the fuel crisis.
fee_notes: Fee set by the Cuban consulate and varies: Cuba's Prague consular office lists 750 CZK and its mission in Trinidad and Tobago lists 108.00 TTD for the online tourist visa; I could not open a fee page for this nationality, so confirm the price with the Cuban embassy, your airline or evisacuba.cu.

conditions_text: Cuba side: Cuban sources set the same tourist-visa rules for all foreign tourists and do not carve out US passports. You need the electronic tourist visa (evisacuba.cu, or the Cuban consulate), whose 10-character code you enter into the D'Viajeros online entry form (dviajeros.mitrans.gob.cu) to get a QR code for arrival; the tourist visa is single entry and Cuban embassy pages give 90 days (extendable) for the online visa, with older pages giving 30 days plus a 30-day extension, so max_stay_days is left null. Passport valid at least 6 months (Cuban consular guidance). Proof of medical insurance valid for Cuba is expected (Canadian, German and Singapore governments say so); ask your airline, since US-issued health policies are reportedly not recognised (German Federal Foreign Office). US side (OFAC, US Treasury, ofac.treasury.gov/faqs/698, released 8 Nov 2017): the FAQ 'Is travel to Cuba for tourist activities permitted?' answers 'No.' and states that travel-related transactions involving Cuba are only permitted for the 12 categories of activities identified in the CACR. OFAC FAQ 695 (updated 29 Sept 2026) lists the 12 categories (family visits, official government business, journalistic activity, professional research, educational activities, religious activities, amateur athletic competitions, support for the Cuban people, humanitarian projects, private foundation and research or educational institute activities, exchange of information or informational materials, and certain authorized export transactions), and says that changes took effect 30 Sept 2026, including removal of the authorization for group people-to-people educational travel. OFAC FAQ 724 states 'The provision of services related to travel for tourist activities or other unauthorized travel to Cuba remains prohibited.' The UK FCDO page also says US rules do not authorise tourist travel from the US to Cuba. I could not open the US State Department Cuba pages (access blocked), so nothing here is taken from them. This is a US legal matter: read the OFAC pages and take advice before booking. NextStamp does not give legal advice.
fee_notes: Fee set by the Cuban consulate and varies: Cuba's Prague consular office lists 750 CZK and its mission in Trinidad and Tobago lists 108.00 TTD for the online tourist visa; I could not open a fee page for this nationality, so confirm the price with the Cuban embassy, your airline or evisacuba.cu.

conditions_text: UK FCDO: tourists need a tourist visa (tourist card) before travelling; apply through the Cuban Embassy in the UK, a travel agent or tour operator, or the eVisa-Cuba site. An approved eVisa gives a ten-character code, entered on the D'Viajeros platform; the eVisa is linked to your passport. Complete the D'Viajeros online arrival form within 72 hours before entering Cuba (FCDO wording); you get a QR code by email to show on arrival, electronically or printed, and airlines check it at check-in. FCDO: passport expiry at least 6 months after arrival (and valid 3 months after planned departure); proof of onward or return travel is required; it does not state a maximum stay, so max_stay_days is null (Cuban embassy pages give 90 days extendable for the online visa; older pages give 30 days plus 30). FCDO does not mention medical insurance on the entry page, but other governments and Cuba expect it (see Canada, Germany). Catch: FCDO currently advises against all but essential travel to Cuba (power-grid failures, fuel rationing, airlines suspending flights); overstaying a visa can lead to detention.
fee_notes: Fee set by the Cuban consulate and varies: Cuba's Prague consular office lists 750 CZK and its mission in Trinidad and Tobago lists 108.00 TTD for the online tourist visa; I could not open a fee page for this nationality, so confirm the price with the Cuban embassy, your airline or evisacuba.cu.

conditions_text: Global Affairs Canada: Canadian tourists need a visa for stays of up to 90 days; tour operators and airlines with direct flights from Canada usually include it in packages. If you travel through a third country, including on a connecting flight, you must get the Cuban electronic visa in advance and enter its 10-character code on the online customs form. You can stay up to 6 months but must apply for an extension to stay beyond the initial 90 days. Complete the online D'Viajeros form up to 72 hours before arrival; a QR code is emailed and must be shown at check-in and on arrival. Regular Canadian passport must be valid for your entire stay. Proof of medical insurance is required on arrival; if you cannot show it you may have to buy limited Cuban coverage at the airport. Officials may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation. Catches: Global Affairs Canada notes that all Canadian airlines have suspended service to Cuba until further notice (international airlines still operate, flights may be cut at short notice) and warns of long unpredictable power cuts and fuel shortages.

Submit the D'Viajeros online entry and customs declaration within 48 hours before check-in. Passport, provisional passport or child passport accepted (not the ID card), valid at least 6 months on entry. Valid health insurance for Cuba covering the whole stay is required (German statutory insurance and US policies are not recognised); without proof you must buy Cuban cover at the port of entry. Catch: the Auswaertiges Amt strongly advises against travel to Cuba right now (energy crisis, fuel shortages, flights cancelled, repatriation not guaranteed).

conditions_text: Singapore MFA: Singaporeans can visit Cuba for up to 30 days without a visa. Jamaica's Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency (PICA) Visa Unit country listing (last updated 13 March 2025, the latest list found; note that the list itself is subject to change) is the source for this row. General entry conditions on Jamaica's mission pages: a passport or acceptable travel document, evidence of sufficient funds and a return or round-trip ticket to another country where you are admissible; the Washington embassy page says the passport should have at least six months' validity, while the Ottawa High Commission page says it must be valid for the intended stay, so carry six months. The decision on admission and length of stay rests with the Immigration Officer at the port of entry, and a visa is needed for study, work or residence.

Indian nationals are on the Panamanian embassy's stamped-visa list (visa estampada): you must apply in person at a Panamanian consulate and, once approved, come in person to have the visa stamped in your passport; the embassy page says approval can take up to 30 business days. Without a qualifying US/UK/Canada/Australia/Singapore/Japan/EU visa or residence (see the held-document rules) you cannot simply arrive. A tourist visa is issued for no more than 90 days (Decreto Ejecutivo 320 of 2008, art. 16), so the stay is capped at 90. Entry conditions in Panama's own requirement sheets: a passport or travel document with at least 3 months of validity, proof of funds of at least B/.500 (about US$500; some foreign governments advise carrying US$1,000 or a credit card), and a booked exit from Panama (return or onward ticket).
fee_notes: Panama's tourist-visa requirement sheet lists a B/.50.00 migration service fee; the fee charged by the consulate for the stamped visa was not stated on an official page that could be read.

conditions_text: Indian nationals normally need a Panamanian stamped visa, but under Decreto Ejecutivo 521 of 2018 as amended by Decreto Ejecutivo 196 of 2024, a person of a visa-requiring nationality who holds a valid visa or residence from the United States may enter without a Panamanian visa (Servicio Nacional de Migracion page, and the Embassy of Panama's visa page). The same exemption also applies to holders of a visa or residence from Canada, the United States, Australia, South Korea, Japan, the United Kingdom, Singapore or an EU member state; only one document country is modelled per row here. Catch: the embassy page states the maximum stay under this exemption is 30 days, and says US permanent resident cards are accepted. The original 2018 decree required a multiple-entry visa already used once and valid at least 6 months on arrival; the embassy page prints that text but also shows the 2024 amendment, so it is unclear whether those visa conditions still apply: treat them as required unless a Panamanian consulate confirms otherwise. Entry conditions in Panama's own requirement sheets: a passport or travel document with at least 3 months of validity, proof of funds of at least B/.500 (about US$500; some foreign governments advise carrying US$1,000 or a credit card), and a booked exit from Panama (return or onward ticket).
fee_notes: No fee stated for entry under this exemption.

conditions_text: Group II country on Bolivia's visa-exemption list: a tourist visa is required. Apply at a Bolivian consulate before travel (passport valid 6 months, application form, return/onward ticket or itinerary, hotel booking or invitation letter, proof of funds, photo, yellow fever certificate). Bolivia's Decree DS 4828 (2022) also allows Group II travellers to be issued a tourism entry authorization by Migracion at airport and land-border posts (same requirements as the visa, valid 30 calendar days, extendable up to 60 more days); because the fee and procedure for that border route could not be confirmed from an official page, treat the consulate visa as the safe route and check with the airline before flying. No concession for holders of a US, Schengen or other third-country visa was found in the Bolivian lists, so none is modelled. Stay is 30 calendar days on a visa or entry authorization, extendable at Migracion (up to 60 more days under DS 4828). Passport must be valid at least 6 months from arrival with two blank pages (FCDO); complete the free online SIGEMIG registration before arrival (Global Affairs Canada) and get an entry stamp, because a missing stamp is fined on exit. Immigration may ask for proof of first-night accommodation. Overland, get both exit and entry stamps. State of emergency in force from 20 Jun 2026 to about 17 Dec 2026 with road blockades possible nationwide (German Foreign Office). Yellow fever: sources differ, so carry a certificate. The US CDC (page reviewed 3 Sep 2026) lists it as required for all arriving travellers aged 1 year or over; UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada say it is required if you arrive from a country with yellow fever transmission risk; the German Foreign Office says it is mandatory for entry into the yellow-fever areas (Beni, Pando and parts of Chuquisaca, La Paz, Cochabamba, Tarija and Santa Cruz) and valid from day 10 after the jab. La Paz, Sucre and the altiplano are not risk areas, but a Uyuni-Potosi-Amazon-lowland trip can be.
fee_notes: Consular tourist visa US$30 (Foreign Ministry consular tariff line V-2, 'conforme a normativa vigente y reciprocidad'); the London embassy says it is paid in pounds at the current tariff. Fee for a border entry authorization: not confirmed from an official source. Extension fees not confirmed.

conditions_text: Indian ordinary passports are not on Namibia's visa-exempt list or its visa-on-arrival list, so a visa is needed before travel. India's Ministry of External Affairs lists Namibia under the e-visa facility available to Indian nationals (page data as on 2 February 2026, last updated 27 August 2026), with no stay length or fee given. The Namibian e-visa portal (eservices.mhaiss.gov.na) refused automated access, so the ministry's own conditions for it could not be read here. The Namibian ministry's general requirements: passport valid at least 6 months with 3 blank pages, confirmed return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation, funds and medical/travel insurance, and a printed approved e-visa to show on arrival. Stay length for Indian visitors was not found on any page I could open, so max stay is left null. If the e-visa is refused, the visa can be applied for at a Namibian embassy or High Commission. The visa regime has been in force since 1 April 2025; no date is pending.
fee_notes: The ministry's fact sheet gives N$1,600 (about US$90) for non-African citizens, subject to annual review; the MEA page does not state a fee for Indians, so confirm the amount on the portal.

conditions_text: US citizens need a visa for tourism since 1 April 2025. Apply in advance through Namibia's online visa-on-arrival portal (eservices.mhaiss.gov.na/visaonarrival) and carry a printed approval notice, or buy a tourist visa on arrival at Windhoek (Hosea Kutako), Walvis Bay or high-volume border posts such as Katima Mulilo and Ngoma. The US Embassy says the default period of stay on a visa on arrival is generally 30 days, with up to 90 days possible at the immigration officer's discretion, so check the entry stamp before leaving the counter; the 30-day stay can be extended at the Ministry of Home Affairs in Windhoek. Passport valid at least 6 months beyond planned departure with 3 completely blank pages. Non-tourist visas (work, study, volunteer) must be obtained before travel from a Namibian mission. The visa regime has been in force since 1 April 2025; no date is pending.
fee_notes: N$1,600 (about US$90) for citizens of non-African countries, per the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security (MHAISS) fact sheet, which says fees are subject to annual review. Reports of an extra N$400 for manual (in-person) applications from September 2025 had no effective date and are not confirmed on an official page I could open; check the portal before travel. The US Embassy notice itself does not state a fee.

Citizens of Commonwealth, African Union and La Francophonie member states receive a visa on arrival at Kigali International Airport or a land border with the fee waived, for a 30-day visit; no prior application is needed (Rwanda's immigration directorate, migration.gov.rw; the Rwandan High Commission in London page names India in its fee-waived list). You can also apply in advance online through the government portal Irembo (irembo.gov.rw) - only irembo.gov.rw and migration.gov.rw issue valid online visas; the immigration site warns that agents may overcharge. A longer or multiple-entry visa is a paid product (USD 70 for 90 days, multiple entry) and must be requested from the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration. Passport validity: the Rwandan missions, the UK FCDO, Global Affairs Canada and Germany's Auswaertiges Amt all say at least 6 months beyond the trip (the migration.gov.rw page itself does not state it). Health entry restriction in force (Rwanda Development Board public notice of 25 May 2026; Germany's Auswaertiges Amt page dated 19 October 2026 still lists it): foreign nationals who travelled to, or transited through, the DR Congo in the 30 days before arriving in Rwanda are refused entry (Global Affairs Canada's page, updated 9 September 2026, says 21 days; the stricter 30 days is the figure on the RDB notice, so plan around 30). Rwanda reported no Ebola cases in its own notices; screening is reinforced at Kigali airport and land borders, and tourism continues as usual per RDB. Land crossings to the DRC (Gisenyi-Goma, Cyangugu-Bukavu) are prohibited for most travellers per Global Affairs Canada. Yellow fever certificate only if arriving from a yellow-fever country.
fee_notes: No fee for this passport (fee waived for Commonwealth/AU/La Francophonie nationals for a 30-day visit). Paid options if you want more: multiple-entry 90-day V1 visa USD 70 (Irembo fee list, page modified 12 May 2026). If you pay by mistake at the counter, Irembo says to use the refund QR code at the visa payment counter.

conditions_text: A visa is required for citizens of India, per the official eligibility checker on Ghana's eVisa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.gh, run by the Ghana Immigration Service with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in force today): apply online before travel for a Tourist (B2) or Business (B1) eVisa; there is no visa on arrival or visa-free route for this passport on the portal. Ghana currently issues single-entry eVisas only; the eVisa is valid for 90 days from issue (you must enter within that period) and the immigration officer at the port of entry sets the length of stay, up to a maximum of 60 days (the applicant guide's sample tourist eVisa shows a 30-day stay). Documents for a tourist visa: passport valid at least 6 months from the intended departure date with at least 3 blank pages, a recent photo, confirmed return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation covering the whole stay (or a signed host letter plus host ID), proof of funds (bank or card statement for the last 3 months) and a yellow fever vaccination certificate. Yellow fever: the portal states a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate/card is required for entry into Ghana and may be checked at the port of entry; travellers without it may be referred to airport health officials, including for vaccination (UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada also say proof is required). Catch: an eVisa does not guarantee entry, which stays at the immigration officer's discretion, and the portal says applications cannot be edited or withdrawn after submission. Several unofficial 'Ghana e-visa' sites exist; the official portal is evisa.immigration.gov.gh. The portal's eVisa went live in May 2026 and replaced the older embassy/high-commission process, whose fees differ.
fee_notes: US$260 standard (processed within 96 hours), US$338 priority (48 hours) or US$442 express (5 hours) per application, a flat fee that is not based on nationality (official applicant guide and portal). Fees are generally non-refundable. Only single-entry eVisas are currently issued; the portal does not list a multiple-entry fee, so a multiple-entry price quoted elsewhere is not confirmed here.

conditions_text: Singapore is not in Ghana's visa-required group: the official eligibility checker on the eVisa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.gh, in force today) returns 'Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) required - Asian visa-waiver country', with validity 90 days, single entry, fee free. So Singapore citizens need no visa but must obtain the free ETA online before travel; it is a pre-travel authorisation, not visa-free entry on arrival. Ghana's ETA guide says the maximum permitted stay under the ETA is 90 days from the date of entry. The ETA application asks for passport details and bio-data page scan, a passport-style photo, flight details (airline, flight number, departure city, arrival date), an address in Ghana (hotel or host) and yellow fever vaccination information; the portal lists passport valid at least 6 months. Yellow fever: a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate/card is required for entry into Ghana and may be checked at the port of entry; travellers without one may be referred to airport health officials, including for vaccination. Catch: the eligibility result can change, so re-run the portal's checker before booking; an ETA does not guarantee entry.
fee_notes: The ETA is free of charge (ETA applicant guide and eligibility checker). No fee is charged for a Singapore passport.

conditions_text: The Passport and Immigration Office's 2025 country-wise table lists India as 'No visa required'. The table gives no stay length for any country; the officer sets it at the border, and the office's visa page says a tourist stay of up to six months in a calendar year may be granted case by case. India's own government and the Indian High Commission pages were not reachable, so no 60 or 90 day figure for Indian passports is confirmed here (the UK, Canadian and Australian governments cite under 60 days for their citizens). Everyone must also complete the free Mauritius All-in-One Travel Form with the Health Declaration Form before boarding (the Passport and Immigration Office calls both mandatory and says the Safe Mauritius site asks for proof at boarding; this is a declaration, not an approval you wait for, and it is in force today). The Passport and Immigration Office's travel requirements page also asks for a return ticket, a confirmed hotel booking or a host's sponsorship, enough money for the stay, and a passport valid beyond the intended stay. Catch: since August 2026 foreign nationals who have been in, or transited through, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda or South Sudan in the previous 21 days are temporarily barred from entry. The final decision to admit and the length of stay rest with the immigration officer at the port of entry.
fee_notes: No visa fee: the Passport and Immigration Office states visas and extensions of stay are issued free of charge, and the All-in-One Travel Form is free (Safe Mauritius warns that third parties charging for it are not endorsed).

conditions_text: A visa is required before travel. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs tourist-visa table lists the Indian national passport as 'Required' (not exempt), and an Indian passport is therefore not eligible for the ETA-IL (which is only for visa-exempt countries). Apply for a B/2 tourist visa: the Population and Immigration Authority runs an online eVisa-B2 system, and its home page (update dated 24 June 2025) says a pilot lets Indian and Sri Lankan passport holders residing in India and Sri Lanka apply for a B2 visa on the official site; in some cases you may be required to attend the nearest Israeli consulate. A B/2 visa is generally single-entry and valid for three months from the day it is granted, with the stay (up to 90 days) set by Border Control on arrival; B/2 holders may not work. Documents asked for: passport valid for at least the visa period and no less than the departure date, a recent photo on a white background, a round-trip ticket, health insurance valid in Israel for the whole stay, proof of accommodation (hotel booking or a signed host letter), and proof of funds (3 months of bank statements, a bank approval or similar). Catch: an eVisa-B2 only lets you reach the border; it does not guarantee entry and a border officer can refuse. No documented cascade (for example a US or UK visa replacing the Israeli visa) was found on an Israeli official page, so none is encoded. Visa-required status read on the MFA table on 2026-10-19; the pilot is described as a pilot, so confirm eligibility at the portal.
fee_notes: eVisa-B2 handling fee: 105 NIS, non-refundable (PIBA eVisa-B2 page). No other fee was stated on that page.

conditions_text: No visa is needed for tourism, but since 1 January 2025 a visa-exempt traveller must hold an approved ETA-IL (Electronic Travel Authorization) before starting the journey, so in practice this is a pre-travel online authorisation. The ETA-IL IS in force today (the Population and Immigration Authority's home page, read 2026-10-19, says travellers 'must have a valid visa or ETA-IL approval before starting their journey'). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs tourist-visa table lists the USA national passport as 'Exempted' from a visa, which is what makes you eligible to apply for an ETA-IL. An approved ETA-IL allows stays of up to 90 days per visit and is valid for up to 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever is sooner; a new passport or a change of name, gender or citizenship needs a new ETA-IL. Your passport must be valid for at least three months from your arrival date. Catch: an ETA-IL is not a guarantee of entry; the border officer decides on arrival and can refuse (the UK government notes entry can be refused, for example for publicly calling for a boycott of Israel, and that officials have asked to see personal email or social media and have searched devices). Customs officials may ask for a return or onward ticket (Global Affairs Canada). Entry cards issued on arrival are needed to go on into the West Bank. Dual nationals and people of Palestinian origin may face extra checks; ask the nearest Israeli embassy first. US State Department pages were not read (they block automated fetches); the rule rests on the Israeli sources.
fee_notes: ETA-IL application fee: 25 NIS, non-refundable even if refused (PIBA). Apply on israel-entry.piba.gov.il, ideally at least 72 hours before travel (Global Affairs Canada); decisions are often quick but can take longer.

The ETA-IL IS in force today (the Population and Immigration Authority's home page, read 2026-10-19, says travellers 'must have a valid visa or ETA-IL approval before starting their journey'). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs tourist-visa table lists the Singapore national passport as 'Exempted' from a visa, which is what makes you eligible to apply for an ETA-IL. An approved ETA-IL allows stays of up to 90 days per visit and is valid for up to 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever is sooner; a new passport or a change of name, gender or citizenship needs a new ETA-IL. Your passport must be valid for at least three months from your arrival date. Catch: an ETA-IL is not a guarantee of entry; the border officer decides on arrival and can refuse (the UK government notes entry can be refused, for example for publicly calling for a boycott of Israel, and that officials have asked to see personal email or social media and have searched devices). Customs officials may ask for a return or onward ticket (Global Affairs Canada). Entry cards issued on arrival are needed to go on into the West Bank. Dual nationals and people of Palestinian origin may face extra checks; ask the nearest Israeli embassy first.

conditions_text: Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay visa for Finland: India is listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (nationals who must hold a visa when crossing the external borders of the Member States). A Schengen visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area; apply in advance at the Finnish embassy's visa channel in India and expect to give fingerprints. Finland's own visa pages (um.fi, migri.fi, finlandabroad.fi) returned access errors to me, so the application steps, processing time, appointment arrangements and the document list are NOT verified here; check finlandabroad.fi (Embassy of Finland, New Delhi) before applying. Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid at least 3 months beyond the date you plan to leave the Schengen area (UK FCDO and Canadian government pages for Finland). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt non-EU travellers) is NOT in force today: the European Commission's ETIAS page (home-affairs.ec.europa.eu, page dated 6 October 2025) says it is not in operation and no applications are collected, and that the EU will announce the start date several months ahead; I found no announced start date, and the Canadian government's Finland page (opened 19 October 2026) still says applications are not yet open. Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now; check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change. The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) registers non-EU travellers (fingerprints and photo) at the Schengen border and replaces manual passport stamping (UK FCDO and Canadian government pages for Finland); the Finnish pages that would give Finland's own start date returned access errors, so it is not stated here.
fee_notes: Fee and any outsourcing-partner service charge not verified from an official Finnish page opened for this row; check the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi.

Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa for Slovenia: the Slovenian Embassy in New Delhi's visa page says 'Visa is required' (only diplomatic-passport holders on short stays are excepted). Apply at the embassy or at VFS Global centres in India, at least 15 calendar days before travel and up to six months ahead. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. The embassy lists: passport with at least two empty pages, issued within the last 10 years and valid at least 3 months beyond the planned departure from Schengen; signed application form and recent ICAO-standard photo; fingerprints in person; travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000 valid across Schengen for the whole stay; documents on purpose of travel, means of support and accommodation. Holders of a valid Schengen residence permit or national long-stay visa from another Schengen state are covered by that document (UK FCDO notes time on such documents does not count towards the 90 days). ETIAS is for visa-exempt travellers and does not apply to visa-required nationals; it is also NOT in force today (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked 19 October 2026: not in operation, no applications collected). Non-EU visitors are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System at the border. Visa holders are not guaranteed entry. FCDO says to register with the police within 3 days of arrival (hotels usually do this).
fee_notes: EUR 90 for applicants over 12 and EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 12 (Embassy New Delhi fee list); VFS service charges are extra and not stated on the embassy page. Some applicants are exempt from the visa fee.

conditions_text: No visa needed for tourism in Romania for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Romania is in the Schengen area (stated on the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada Romania pages), so the 90 days are counted across all Schengen countries combined and time in other Schengen states counts. The count starts at your first entry; if you return within 180 days you only get the days remaining. You may be asked for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. The passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and expire at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (UK FCDO). Non-EU travellers are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System (photo and fingerprints, free) on entry. Temporary internal Schengen border checks can be reinstated, so carry your passport on arrival from another Schengen country (Global Affairs Canada). Overstaying can bring an entry ban of up to 3 years (UK FCDO). Source for the visa-free status is Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, which lists the United States among nationalities exempt from the short-stay visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period (the US State Department page returned HTTP 403 and was not read). ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu, opened 19 October 2026) states it is currently not in operation and no applications are collected, and that the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. When it starts the same site lists a EUR 20 fee. Do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now.

No visa needed for tourism in Romania for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Romania is in the Schengen area (stated on the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada Romania pages), so the 90 days are counted across all Schengen countries combined and time in other Schengen states counts. The count starts at your first entry; if you return within 180 days you only get the days remaining. You may be asked for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. The passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and expire at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (UK FCDO). Non-EU travellers are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System (photo and fingerprints, free) on entry. Temporary internal Schengen border checks can be reinstated, so carry your passport on arrival from another Schengen country (Global Affairs Canada). Overstaying can bring an entry ban of up to 3 years (UK FCDO). Source for the visa-free status is Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, which lists Australia among nationalities exempt from the short-stay visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period (Smartraveller timed out when fetched, so the Australian government's own wording was not read). The EU Entry/Exit System applies only to non-EU nationals and ETIAS is for visa-exempt non-EU travellers (and is not in operation today), so neither affects German citizens.

Ordinary Indian passports need a visa before travel (the Albanian foreign ministry's country table marks India 'WITH VISA' for ordinary passports, and India's MEA lists Albania under countries that provide an e-Visa facility to Indian nationals). Apply for the short-stay Type C visa on the official portal e-visa.al; the ministry names it as the only official site. Type C allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period from first entry. The Albanian embassy FAQ says visa evaluation takes 15-30 working days, so apply well ahead. Indians who hold certain other visas or residence permits need no Albanian visa: see the cascade rows (valid multiple-entry US, UK or Schengen/EU visa that has already been used, a residence permit from those places, or a 10-year UAE residence permit). Passport: valid at least 3 months beyond the visa term with at least 2 blank pages. Not covered by Albania's 2026 temporary tourist waiver (that applies to Saudi Arabia and Qatar only).
fee_notes: Type C fee EUR 15 for single, double or multiple entry, per the ministry's country table; children aged 0 to 6 free and 7 to 12 half the adult fee. Fees can change; confirm on e-visa.al.

conditions_text: Indian ordinary passports normally need an Albanian visa, but a foreign national holding a valid multiple-entry US visa that has already been used in the US, or a valid US residence permit, may enter Albania without a visa (Albanian foreign ministry, as repeated on the Albanian embassy FAQ). The ministry says this exemption does not apply to Iranian nationals. The page gives no separate stay length for this route, so max stay is left null; do not assume 90 days. Carry the visa or permit and the passport it is in. The live ministry page (punetejashtme.gov.al) blocked automated fetching, so this is read from the Albanian embassy FAQ at ambasadat.gov.al, which matches the ministry page snapshot of 1 October 2026.

No visa needed. The US Embassy in Tirana says US citizens do not need a visa and generally may stay up to one year without a residence permit; to restart the one-year clock you must leave Albania and stay out for at least 90 days (shorter trips abroad do not reset it). The Albanian foreign ministry's country table marks the USA 'WITHOUT VISA' but does not itself state the one-year length, and the embassy page notes officers may deny entry or limit the stay at their discretion, so the stamp or entry record you receive is what counts. The embassy asks for a passport with at least 3 months' validity (it recommends 6) and says officers may ask for a return ticket, proof of accommodation or other proof of purpose. Anything longer than a year, or working or studying, needs a residence permit. Albania is not in the Schengen Area, so ETIAS does not apply to a trip that only visits Albania.

Longer stays need a long-stay visa or residence permit. Albania is not in the Schengen Area, so ETIAS does not apply to a trip that only visits Albania.

Montenegro is not in the EU or Schengen area, so ETIAS does not apply to entry into Montenegro. Montenegro's government announced on 27 July 2026 that, as the last step of aligning its visa policy with the EU, nationals of Belarus, China, Russia, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye need a visa from 1 November 2026; nationals of this passport are not on that list. Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa for Bulgaria: India is listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, the list of countries whose nationals must hold a visa to cross the EU's external borders (Commission-hosted copy of the regulation, original 2018 text, opened 19 October 2026), and VFS Global, the application partner for Bulgaria in India, runs a Bulgaria visa page for Indian applicants. The Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs type C visa guidance (mfa.bg PDF) says a C visa covers a total stay of up to 90 days within each 6 months from the first entry. It lists as documents: passport, photo, documents supporting the purpose of travel, funds of at least EUR 50 per day of stay (minimum EUR 500) or prepaid services, accommodation funds or proof of prepaid accommodation or an invitation-declaration, proof of means to leave the country or a ticket, and travel insurance valid in the EU with at least EUR 30,000 cover including repatriation and emergency treatment. VFS Global's India page for Bulgaria adds: passport valid at least 3 months beyond departure, issued within the last 10 years and with two blank facing pages; applications cannot be lodged more than 3 months before departure and take around 15 working days (apply well before 15 calendar days; some cases take longer). Holders of a valid Schengen residence permit or long-stay visa of another Schengen state can travel on that document. A visa does not guarantee entry. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is also not in force today (Global Affairs Canada, 13 October 2026: applications not yet open). Non-EU travellers are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System at the border. The Bulgarian MFA visa pages were blocked by a bot check, so country-specific details not in the MFA PDF or VFS page were not confirmed; check the Bulgarian Embassy in New Delhi before applying.
fee_notes: VFS Global India lists a visa fee of INR 9,900 (no fee for children aged 12 and under) plus a VFS service charge of INR 2,530 and optional extras (VFS India page for Bulgaria, opened 19 October 2026); fees are non-refundable. Confirm with the Bulgarian Embassy in New Delhi.

Bulgaria is a full member of the Schengen area (stated on the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada Bulgaria pages), so the 90 days are counted across all Schengen countries combined, and days already spent in other Schengen states in the previous 180 days count. Passport rules (UK FCDO): issued less than 10 years before arrival and valid at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area. Border officers may ask for proof of accommodation, travel insurance, a return or onward ticket and sufficient funds (FCDO, Global Affairs Canada). Overstaying can bring a ban of up to 3 years (FCDO). Declare cash or travellers' cheques of EUR 10,000 or more (FCDO). Non-EU travellers are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System on entry (photo and fingerprints, no charge; FCDO, Global Affairs Canada). Temporary internal Schengen border checks can be reinstated, so carry your passport when arriving from another Schengen country. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: Global Affairs Canada's Bulgaria page (updated 13 October 2026) says ETIAS applications are not yet open, and the EU has said it will announce the start date several months in advance. Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now; when it starts it becomes a required pre-travel authorisation.

EU freedom of movement: German citizens can enter and travel in Bulgaria with a valid passport or a valid national identity card (the Your Europe portal says the document must be valid on the day of travel). No visa applies and the 90-in-180 limit does not apply to EU citizens. The EU Entry/Exit System applies only to non-EU nationals and ETIAS is for visa-exempt non-EU travellers (and is not in operation today), so neither affects German citizens. Temporary internal Schengen border checks can occur, so carry the document. Stays beyond three months may bring a local registration duty that was not checked for this record.

Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay (C) visa for tourism in Estonia; ordinary Indian passports are not on the Ministry's visa-exempt list (it names India only for diplomatic, service, official and special passports). Lodge the application at least 15 days before travel and no earlier than six months before (Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Photo and 10 fingerprints are taken at lodging (not repeated if given less than 59 months earlier). Normal decision within 15 days, extendable to 45 days. Visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. Requirements: passport issued within the previous 10 years, valid at least three months beyond departure from Schengen, two blank pages; travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000 valid in all Schengen states; proof of funds, which the Ministry sets at EUR 70 per day of stay in Estonia. Where to lodge in India (embassy or the VFS centre Estonia uses in India) was not confirmed from an official page this run: check vm.ee. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, EUR 20) is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked 19 October 2026) states it is currently not in operation, no applications are collected, and the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now; check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking because this is expected to change. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities.
fee_notes: State fee EUR 90 for adults; EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 11; free under 6 (Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Not refunded on refusal. A service-provider fee may be charged separately where a visa centre is used; its amount was not confirmed.

German citizens are EU citizens and enter and stay in Estonia under EU freedom of movement: no visa, no ETIAS, no 90-day limit (Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists EU/EEA nationals as not needing a visa). Both Germany and Estonia are in the Schengen area, so there are no routine internal border checks, but you must carry a valid passport or national ID card; driving licences and bank or other cards are not accepted as travel documents.

Indian ordinary passport holders are not on the Latvian foreign ministry's visa-exempt list (India appears there only for diplomatic passports), so a Schengen short-stay visa must be obtained before travel. The Embassy of Latvia in New Delhi says Schengen visa applications are submitted through VFS Global visa application centres, which forward them to the embassy for assessment; its stated target is 10 days from the embassy receiving the application, and up to 30 days if more documents are requested or an interview is scheduled. Apply to Latvia if it is your only or main destination (longest stay), or the country of first entry if there is no main destination. A short-stay visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Latvia-specific catch: Latvia's Electronic Travel Declaration (eta.gov.lv, in force since 1 September 2025) must be submitted at least 48 hours before arrival; it is waived only for a visa or residence permit issued by Latvia, so an Indian citizen holding a Schengen visa issued by another country must still submit it (eta.gov.lv). It is not an entry permit. Passport: UK FCDO's Latvia page states it must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (not stated on the embassy page). Travel medical insurance valid across the Schengen area is generally required for a visa application (not stated on the embassy page; confirm with VFS). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is NOT in force today (the official ETIAS site, checked 2026-10-19, says it is 'currently not in operation').
fee_notes: The embassy page states no fee amount, only that fees are non-refundable and documents (other than the passport) are not returned. A search snippet of the VFS Latvia India page reported EUR 90 for adults (EUR 45 for ages 6-12) plus a VFS service charge of INR 2,999, but that VFS page returned 403 when opened, so these figures are not confirmed from an opened page; check VFS Global before applying.

EU freedom of movement: German citizens can enter and travel in Latvia with either a valid passport or a valid national identity card, valid on the day of travel (Your Europe, europa.eu). Carry the document: Schengen states can apply temporary border controls; Your Europe says you must show a valid passport or ID card when a country applies them. ETIAS is not in force today (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked 2026-10-19) and would not apply to EU citizens anyway.

Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa for tourism in Lithuania: India is on the visa-required list (Annex I) of EU Regulation 2018/1806 (European Commission home-affairs site). Apply in advance through a Lithuanian mission that handles applications from India; the visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Passport must be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area and issued within the previous 10 years (UK FCDO states both parts for Lithuania; Global Affairs Canada states the 3-month part; Lithuania's own foreign ministry pages block automated fetches, so these foreign-government pages are the fallback sources for the passport rule). Lithuanian mission pages (mfa.lt) and the VFS page blocked automated fetches, so appointment channel, fee, insurance amount and processing time were NOT verified here: check the Lithuanian embassy in New Delhi before applying. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today: the official ETIAS site (travel-europe.europa.eu), checked 2026-10-19, says it is 'currently not in operation' and no applications are collected. The EU Entry/Exit System registers fingerprints and a photo of non-EU visitors at the Schengen external border (UK FCDO: 'EES is now being implemented across the Schengen area'; no Lithuania-specific start date found).

Indian citizens with ordinary passports need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa for Slovakia. The Slovak Embassy in New Delhi says it works with BLS International and that appointment slots for type C applications are booked on the BLS Slovakia-India website (Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore centres); the applicant must attend in person and agents are not allowed. (The embassy page mzv.sk/dilli-en blocks automated fetches, so this wording was read from a search-result excerpt of that page and should be re-checked.) Per the European Commission: apply at least 15 days and no earlier than 6 months before travel; normal processing is 15 days and can stretch to 45; fingerprints are taken at submission; you need medical insurance covering emergency care, hospitalisation and repatriation. The embassy says processing starts when it has the full file, fingerprints and fee. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area; holding a visa does not guarantee entry. Passport issued within the previous 10 years and valid at least 3 months beyond departure from Schengen. ETIAS is for visa-exempt travellers and does not apply to visa-required nationals; it is also NOT in force today (travel-europe.europa.eu describes it as not in operation; see EU reporting of August 2026). Non-EU visitors are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System at the border. Hotels register guests with the police; in private accommodation register within 3 working days.
fee_notes: EUR 90 for adults and EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 11 (European Commission, since 11 June 2024; children under 6 are exempt); the BLS service fee is charged on top and was not confirmed. The embassy's own fee page, as indexed in search results, still showed the older EUR 80/40, so rely on the Commission figure and confirm at booking.

conditions_text: No visa is needed for tourism in Slovakia. The US Commercial Service's Slovakia guide (trade.gov) says US citizens may enter for up to 90 days for tourist or business purposes without a visa and that stays beyond 90 days in any 6-month period need a temporary residence permit; the Schengen 90-in-180 rule applies across all Schengen countries together. That guide advises US passports valid at least six months beyond the stay, while the Schengen rule (UK FCDO) is 3 months beyond departure, issued within 10 years: use the stricter six months to be safe, and note an airline can apply its own rule. The passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid at least 3 months beyond the planned departure from Schengen (UK FCDO). Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket, proof of funds and proof of accommodation. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, EUR 20 fee once it starts) is NOT in force today: the EU's official Travel to Europe site describes it as currently not in operation with no applications collected, and reporting dated 11 August 2026 says the EU dropped its earlier Q4 2026 target and will announce a start date several months ahead (the Commission's own April 2026 news item still said Q4 2026, so it is superseded). Do not pay any site claiming to issue ETIAS now; check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking. Non-EU visitors are registered in the EU Entry/Exit System (fingerprints and photo, free) on first entry; it has been fully operational since 10 April 2026, so allow extra time at the border. Hotels register guests with the police; in private accommodation, register at the Foreigners Police within 3 working days of arrival (UK FCDO). Temporary internal Schengen border checks can occur, so carry your passport. Declare cash of EUR 10,000 or more.

Indian ordinary passport holders need a Cyprus short-stay (Category C) visa before travel: India is not on the Cypriot Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries whose nationals are exempt (only Indian diplomatic, official and service passports are exempt). Apply through the High Commission of Cyprus in New Delhi: by appointment (delhi.consulate@mfa.gov.cy) and, under a six-month contract effective 21 July 2026, through VFS Global (visa.vfsglobal.com/ind/en/cyp) in 19 Indian cities. Applications can be lodged up to six months ahead and no later than 15 calendar days before travel. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Requirements include a passport issued within 10 years, valid 3 months beyond the visa, with 2 blank pages; travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000; accommodation proof, flight reservation, funds and employment proof. Cascade: holders of a valid double or multiple-entry Schengen (Category C) visa, or a national visa or residence permit of a Schengen state, need no separate Cyprus visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period (Cyprus applies EU Decision 565/2014/EU); the New Delhi page also lists other EU residence permits. This is modelled in this record only as text (Schengen visas are not per-country held documents in the app); the Schengen visa must be multiple-entry and valid. No Cyprus e-visa or pre-arrival permit for Indian tourists was found on the official pages read.
fee_notes: Short-stay visa fee EUR 90 (children 6-12 EUR 45, under 6 free), paid in cash in euro per the New Delhi High Commission page; non-refundable if refused. VFS service fee EUR 2.6 excluding GST, plus optional services.

conditions_text: Cyprus is an EU member but is not in the Schengen area, and has its own entry rules: the Cypriot Ministry of Foreign Affairs list (the United States of America is on it) exempts nationals of the United States of America from a visa for up to 90 days, provided they are bona fide visitors. The list page is dated 9 June 2024 on gov.cy; the later gov.cy visas page still points to the same exemption list. Cyprus's 90 days are counted separately from Schengen stays (UK FCDO: Schengen visits do not count toward the Cyprus limit or vice versa). Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. Passport: UK FCDO says it must have been issued within 10 years of arrival, be valid at least 3 months after departure and have a blank page; Global Affairs Canada says 6 months, so carry a passport with 6 months to be safe. No pre-arrival authorisation (no visa-style permit, no CYPASS-type form) is required for these passports on the official pages read. ETIAS is not in force today (Global Affairs Canada page updated 11 August 2026: not yet open for applications) and Cyprus is not in Schengen. Enter through the Republic's ports and airports: entering the island via the north (Ercan airport, Famagusta port) is treated as illegal entry by the Republic and can lead to a fine or refusal; time spent in the north counts toward the 90 days (UK FCDO).

Canadian citizens need no visa for tourist or business stays of up to 90 days in Cyprus (Global Affairs Canada, page last updated 11 August 2026; the Cypriot Ministry of Foreign Affairs exemption list, dated 9 June 2024 on gov.cy, also lists Canada). Global Affairs Canada says a regular Canadian passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond the planned departure; the UK FCDO's Cyprus page (for its own citizens) says 3 months, so follow the stricter 6 months. Customs may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. Cyprus is not in Schengen, and the UK FCDO page says Schengen visits do not count toward the Cyprus limit or vice versa. No pre-arrival authorisation is required. ETIAS is not yet open for applications (Global Affairs Canada), and Canadian dual nationals of participating countries cannot use it. Entering the island through northern Cyprus (Ercan airport, Famagusta port) is illegal under the Republic's law and may prevent you later crossing the UN buffer zone; time in the north counts toward the 90 days (UK FCDO). Dual citizens aged 16+ or eligible for Cypriot citizenship may need an exit permit from Cyprus's Ministry of Defence.

German citizens are EU citizens and need no visa for Cyprus under EU freedom of movement. The Cypriot government's visas page states that citizens of all EU Member States can enter Cyprus with their identity card, as long as it bears the holder's photo; a valid passport is also accepted. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs exemption list (dated 9 June 2024) repeats this and lists Germany. No pre-arrival authorisation is required. Cyprus is not in the Schengen area, so you are still checked at the border on arrival, even from another EU state. Rules for staying longer than three months (EU registration) were not checked on an official page for this record. Enter via the Republic's own airports and ports: arriving via northern Cyprus is treated by the Republic as illegal entry (UK FCDO).

Indian citizens are on the Maltese list of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of a visa when crossing the external borders (Identita Malta, official PDF). For tourism you need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa obtained in advance. Identita states type C visas are processed only by Maltese missions or foreign representations (not by Identita), in your country of residence, and that a type C visa is for short visits of not more than 90 days; the Schengen limit is 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries combined. Passport issued within the previous 10 years and valid at least 3 months after leaving Schengen (UK FCDO Schengen rule, fallback; Malta's pages did not state it). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS site (travel-europe.europa.eu), checked 19 Oct 2026, says it is 'currently not in operation'. Not verified here: the Maltese-side office or VFS channel serving India, processing time and the service fee. Check the Maltese mission or representing Schengen state before applying; holding a visa does not guarantee entry.

Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of enough money for the stay (FCDO). India is not on Mongolia's visa-free lists (the Ministry of Foreign Affairs list shows India visa-free only for diplomatic and official passports). Indian ordinary-passport holders are on the Immigration Authority's e-visa country list (entry 92) and can apply online at evisa.mn without visiting an embassy: K2 (tourist) allows a stay of up to 30 days; K6 (transit) up to 10 days. The Mongolian embassy in Geneva states e-visas are emailed within 72 hours; carry a printed or digital copy. The Immigration Authority's duration table gives 150 days validity for transit visas; K2 validity is not stated on the pages read.
fee_notes: Mongolian embassy tariff (Geneva page dated 2026-07-01, rate valid through 2026) lists US$50 for a single-entry visa; evisa.mn shows the exact amount at payment and the fee is non-refundable. Fee for Indian applicants specifically was not confirmed on a page naming India.

conditions_text: US citizens with any passport type may enter Mongolia without a visa for up to 90 days (the Ministry of Foreign Affairs list shows 90 days, in effect since 2001). This is a standing arrangement, not part of the temporary 2026 exemption. Stays over 30 days must be registered with Mongolia's Immigration Authority (the Mongolian embassy in Washington says within 7 days). A longer stay needs a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-free entry.

fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-free entry. If the exemption lapses, an e-visa (K2, up to 30 days) would be needed; Mongolian embassy tariff lists US$50 single entry.

conditions_text: Indian citizens do not need a visa; they need an Entry Permit instead (Embassy of India, Thimphu: 'No Visa is required to visit Bhutan'; Tourism Council of Bhutan: Indian nationals apply for a permit rather than a visa). Accepted travel document: a valid Indian passport (the embassy says at least 6 months' validity) or an original Voter Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India, plus recent passport-size photographs; minors under 18 without a passport need an original birth certificate, and under-18s must be accompanied by a legal guardian (embassy page and bhutan.travel/faqs). The permit can be applied for online in advance, through a tour operator or hotel, or at the point of entry; applying on arrival may involve a long wait (bhutan.travel/visa). By road the permit is issued by the regional immigration office at the Indo-Bhutan border (the embassy lists Phuentsholing, Gelephu, Samdrup Jongkhar and Samtse); by air it is issued at Paro International Airport. Catch: the embassy's tourism page (last updated 12 October 2026) says the Entry Permit covers Thimphu and Paro only, and travel beyond them needs a special area permit from the Immigration office in Thimphu; bhutan.travel/faqs says route permits are no longer required for most visitors travelling with a certified guide, so confirm for your itinerary. A certified guide must accompany visitors at all times per bhutan.travel/faqs. No maximum stay is stated on the pages read, so max_stay_days is left null.
fee_notes: No visa fee and no fee payable in advance for the permit (bhutan.travel/visa). Indian nationals pay a Sustainable Development Fee of Nu. 1,200 (or the INR equivalent) per person per night; children aged 6 to under 12 pay Nu./INR 600 per night and children under 6 pay nothing (bhutan.travel/faqs). The Indian embassy page lists INR 1,200 per day. Border-town 24-hour stays in Samtse, Phuentsholing, Gelephu and Samdrupjongkhar within designated zones are SDF-free from 2 June 2026 to August 2027 (bhutan.travel/faqs). The embassy also states Indian currency limits for carrying in: notes up to Rs. 500 denominations with a total limit of Rs. 25,000; amounts above that only in Rs. 100 denominations or lower.

conditions_text: A visa is required before travel; there is no visa-free entry for this passport. Apply online through the Department of Immigration portal (immi.gov.bt) yourself or through a tour operator or hotel, then pay the visa fee and the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) with the application (Tourism Council of Bhutan, bhutan.travel/visa). You need a digital copy of a valid passport, a recent digital passport photo, arrival and departure dates and payment details; applications are reviewed within five working days. The UK FCDO adds that the visa is pre-approved and issued on arrival, and that the border officer should stamp it in your passport. Stay is limited to 90 days from entry (bhutan.travel/faqs). Passport must be valid at least 6 months after your planned departure (UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada; the Tourism Council pages do not state a validity rule). Independent travel is limited: bhutan.travel/faqs says all aspects of a trip may be booked independently but a guide certified by the Department of Tourism must accompany visitors at all times, including those driving their own car, and treks must be arranged through an accredited operator; Global Affairs Canada's older wording says tours must be pre-arranged through an authorized agency. In practice most visitors book through a licensed Bhutanese tour operator.
fee_notes: Visa application fee US$40, one-off and non-refundable (bhutan.travel/visa; UK FCDO). Sustainable Development Fee US$100 per adult per night, paid with the application (bhutan.travel/faqs); children aged 6 to under 12 pay US$50 per night and children under 6 pay no SDF (bhutan.travel/faqs). The Tourism Council's visa page says US$100 'per day'. An older tourism.gov.bt Q&A page still shows US$200 a night; that is outdated against the two Tourism Council pages and the UK FCDO. From 2 June 2026 for a year (to August 2027), visitors staying 24 hours in the border towns Samtse, Phuentsholing, Gelephu or Samdrupjongkhar within designated zones pay no SDF (bhutan.travel/faqs).

conditions_text: Indian ordinary-passport holders can enter Kazakhstan without a visa for up to 14 days per stay, which is shorter than the 30 days given to US, UK, Canadian, Australian, German, Singapore and Brazilian passports. The Foreign Ministry table (updated 21 August 2026) shows 'visa-free up to 14 days' for India; India's MEA list (page footer updated 27 August 2026) also shows Kazakhstan at 14 days, non-extendable. The Kazakh embassy announcement of the July 2022 regime (Decree 464, covers private, tourist and business trips) adds that the total visa-free stay is capped at 42 days within any 180-day period. For a longer stay, or if you prefer a visa, Kazakhstan lists India among the countries whose citizens can get a single-entry e-visa (business, tourist or medical), but it is issued only against a valid invitation number from a Kazakh host approved by the migration service, via the Visa and Migration Portal (vmp.gov.kz), is valid only for the applicant, and can be used only at international airports (the Kazakh embassy page names Astana and Almaty). The e-visa stay length is not stated on the pages read. No special concession for Indian passport holders who hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visa was found in the Foreign Ministry pages or on India's MEA list (the MEA list notes such conditions only for other countries), so none is encoded. Registration with migration authorities is required (hotel or host, within 3 working days per FCDO). Passport validity: Global Affairs Canada's general rule is at least 3 months beyond departure with one blank page; the e-visa page asks for at least 2 clean pages and validity 3 months beyond the visa. QazETA (the electronic travel authorisation for visa-free visitors) is not mandatory today per Global Affairs Canada (voluntary and free, updated 15 October 2026); FCDO says it is expected to become mandatory for visa-free travellers from November 2026, so check the official QazETA portal and whether it will apply to Indian passports before you fly.
fee_notes: No fee for visa-free entry. E-visa consular fee, as the sources differ: Kazakhstan's embassy in Kuala Lumpur (Nov 2023) says 80 USD for a single-entry e-visa; the embassy in the UK (page updated Sept 2024) lists 60 USD for a tourist e-visa and 80 USD for business or medical. Consular fees are non-refundable. Confirm the amount on vmp.gov.kz before paying. QazETA is currently free.

conditions_text: USA ordinary-passport holders can enter Kazakhstan without a visa for up to 30 days per stay for tourism or business. The US State Department page was not consulted; the stay is from the Kazakh Foreign Ministry table. Rule as stated in the Kazakh Foreign Ministry's visa-regime table for ordinary passports (page updated 21 August 2026; read through the gov.kz content API because the page itself renders blank to fetchers). The UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada pages both say the total visa-free stay cannot exceed 90 days in any 180-day period, and that your hotel or host must register your arrival with migration authorities (FCDO: within 3 working days); Canada says registration still applies even with an ETA. Passport validity: Global Affairs Canada says at least 3 months beyond the date you expect to leave and at least one blank page; FCDO says at least 30 days from arrival (3 months beyond a visa's expiry if you hold one), so carry 3 months to be safe. QazETA, Kazakhstan's electronic travel authorisation for visa-free visitors, is NOT mandatory today (Global Affairs Canada, updated 15 October 2026: voluntary and free, apply at least 72 hours ahead, valid 180 days); FCDO says it is expected to become mandatory for visa-free travellers from November 2026 under new regulations, and later press reports give a different phased timeline, so check the official QazETA portal before you fly. Yellow fever certificate only if arriving from a risk country (FCDO).
fee_notes: No fee for visa-free entry. QazETA is currently free (Global Affairs Canada); FCDO says a fee of about 7 to 15 pounds may be introduced later.

Global Affairs Canada (updated 15 October 2026) confirms no visa for up to 30 days; student travel requires a visa. Rule as stated in the Kazakh Foreign Ministry's visa-regime table for ordinary passports (page updated 21 August 2026; read through the gov.kz content API because the page itself renders blank to fetchers). conditions_text: India is on the Embassy in India's own e-visa page. No special concession for Indian passport holders was found on any official page: they use the same standard e-visa as other nationals and are not in the visa-free list. Azerbaijan issues an ASAN Visa e-visa (apply online at evisa.gov.az, which blocks automated fetches, so the details here come from Azerbaijani embassy pages). The Embassy of Azerbaijan in India states: standard e-visa issued within 3 working days; e-visas valid for 30 days. The Embassy in Australia states the e-visa 'determines the duration of stay in the country up to 30 days' and lists this nationality among countries eligible for an e-visa. UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada both describe it as normally single entry, allowing a 30-day visit within a 90-day validity period, and say to print it and carry it with the passport. UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada both advise a passport valid at least 6 months after arrival with 2 blank pages (confirm the rule that applies to your nationality). Stays over 15 days require registration with the State Migration Service. Global Affairs Canada says land borders are closed to Canadian travellers except for freight, so plan to enter by air. There is no visa on arrival at Baku airport.
fee_notes: Standard e-visa state fee USD 20 (Azerbaijan embassies in India and Australia). An urgent 3-hour option costs more (USD 60 per the Embassy in New Delhi). The portal may add its own service charge; not confirmed from an official page.
