conditions_text: The Azerbaijan Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa-free list (group IV, unilateral regime for ordinary passports) shows Singapore: visa-free from 1 August 2026 to 1 August 2027, up to 3 times and up to 30 days per entry. Press reports (APA, Trend) describe it as for tourism and say other purposes, or staying beyond the permitted period, need a visa in advance. The regime is dated and ends 1 August 2027 unless extended. Singapore is also on the e-visa list of older embassy pages, so an e-visa remains an option. Stays over 15 days require registration with the State Migration Service.

Indian ordinary-passport holders need a visa before travelling. India's Ministry of External Affairs list of countries that give Indians visa-free, visa-on-arrival or e-visa access (updated 27 Aug 2026, data as of 2 Feb 2026) does not include Tunisia, and MEA's visa-exemption table for Tunisia covers only diplomatic and official/special passports (90 days). Apply to the Embassy of Tunisia in New Delhi or a consulate before departure; the embassy's own page could not be read for the document list, so confirm requirements with it. No Tunisian e-visa or visa-on-arrival for Indians was found. Press reports (2014, 2018) mention a concession for prepaid group tours; no official Tunisian or Indian page confirming it could be read, so do not plan around it. Border officers can ask for return tickets and proof of accommodation (per FCDO advice for all visitors). Passport validity: not stated by an official source read; carry at least 6 months to be safe (Canada's advice, and Germany's, both say 6 months).
fee_notes: Visa fee not confirmed from an official page; ask the Embassy of Tunisia in New Delhi (Vasant Vihar address from an older embassy page; confirm). Tunisia levies a hotel tax on arrival of 8 TND (3-star) or 12 TND (4-5 star) per person per night, up to ten nights (per FCDO).

conditions_text: Tunisian consular pages list US citizens among the nationalities exempt from a visa for tourist stays of up to three months (page undated and could not be opened directly in this check, text seen through a search extract, so confirm with the Embassy of Tunisia in Washington before booking). The US State Department pages for Tunisia returned an access error (403) and could not be read. Other Tunisian-list nationalities are confirmed at 90 days by FCDO (UK), Global Affairs Canada, Smartraveller (Australia) and Singapore MFA. Border officers can ask for return tickets and proof of accommodation (per FCDO advice for all visitors); a few visitors have been refused entry for lacking accommodation proof. Passport validity: Canada advises 6 months beyond departure and Germany 6 months on arrival; no US official source was read, so carry 6 months.
fee_notes: No visa fee for the exempt stay. Hotel tax payable on arrival: 8 TND per person per night in 3-star and 12 TND in 4-5 star hotels, up to ten nights (per FCDO). Overstay fines apply (per FCDO).

conditions_text: No visa is needed for stays of up to 90 days. Your passport should be valid for the duration of your stay. Border officials stamp the passport on arrival and check the stay on departure; overstaying can bring a fine payable at the airport. Officials can ask for onward or return tickets, contact details and proof of accommodation, and a small number of visitors have been refused entry or delayed for lacking accommodation evidence. Tunisia has strict currency controls and a foreign-currency declaration is required on arrival.
fee_notes: No visa fee. Hotel tax payable on arrival: 8 TND per person per night at 3-star hotels and 12 TND at 4- and 5-star hotels, for a maximum of ten nights (per FCDO). Tunisian dinars cannot be taken out of the country.

conditions_text: A tourist visa is not required for stays up to 90 days (Global Affairs Canada also lists no business or student visa for that period). The passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave Tunisia, and transport companies may apply stricter rules. For stays over 90 days, contact a Tunisian embassy or consulate before departure. Canadians who are also Tunisian citizens may be asked to show their Tunisian passport.
fee_notes: No visa fee. Currency of 20,000 TND or more (equivalent) must be declared on arrival, departure and in transit (per Global Affairs Canada). Hotel tax of 8 or 12 TND per person per night applies on arrival (per FCDO).

conditions_text: Smartraveller says Australian citizens do not need a visa if visiting Tunisia for 90 days or less; for other types of travel a visa must be obtained before arrival. Entry conditions can change at short notice, so confirm with the nearest Tunisian embassy or consulate. Smartraveller's Tunisia page gives no Tunisia-specific passport-validity figure in the text read; Canada and Germany both advise 6 months, so carry 6 months. Officials can ask for return tickets and proof of accommodation (per FCDO advice for all visitors). Note: some older commercial pages claim a visa on arrival for Australians; the official Smartraveller wording above is the one relied on. fee_notes: No visa fee for the exempt stay. Hotel tax of 8 TND (3-star) or 12 TND (4-5 star) per person per night on arrival, up to ten nights (per FCDO).

conditions_text: German citizens need no visa for tourist, private or business stays of up to 120 days (Auswaertiges Amt, page dated 19 Oct 2026; this is longer than the 90 days that applies to UK, Canadian, Australian and Singapore passports). Documents must be valid for at least six months on arrival. A normal passport is accepted; a children's passport is accepted; a provisional passport is accepted only with a return ticket and sufficient funds; the German ID card (Personalausweis) and provisional ID card are NOT accepted for entry. Overstaying 120 days costs 20 TND per five-day period. Tunisia is not in the EU or Schengen area, so EU freedom of movement does not apply.
fee_notes: No visa fee. Hotel tax of 8 TND (3-star) or 12 TND (4-5 star) per person per night on arrival, up to ten nights (per FCDO). Some airports issue a 'carte de visiteur non-resident' that must be kept for departure (per Auswaertiges Amt).

conditions_text: Brazil and Tunisia have a visa-exemption agreement (promulgated in Brazil by Decreto 5.169 of 4 Aug 2004): holders of valid national passports may enter, transit and stay for tourism or business for up to 90 days, renewable provided the total stay does not exceed 180 days a year. The agreement text does not state a passport-validity figure; Canada and Germany advise 6 months, so carry 6 months. Work, study or residence need a separate visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee for the exempt stay. Hotel tax of 8 TND (3-star) or 12 TND (4-5 star) per person per night on arrival, up to ten nights (per FCDO).

conditions_text: Australia is not on the list of nationalities exempt from a Senegalese entry visa. Passport must be valid at least 6 months; carry return/onward travel and accommodation proof; yellow fever certificate if arriving from a risk country. Because the official pages do not state a stay length, max_stay_days is left null.

conditions_text: India: the Indian government's visa-facility list (MEA) shows an e-Tourist Visa at evisa.gov.et (about 3 working days) and also a visa on arrival at Bole airport valid one month, with a passport valid 6 months and the fee paid. I found no Ethiopian page confirming the on-arrival option, and FCDO and Global Affairs Canada tell visitors to get the visa online first, so this row is e-visa; carry the approval rather than relying on arrival. A tourist visa is required and is obtained online through the official Ethiopian e-Visa platform (evisa.gov.et); apply before you travel. FCDO says the standard tourist option is a 30-day single-entry visa (an extension of 30 or 90 days can be requested before expiry, in person at the Immigration and Citizenship Service head office in Addis Ababa) and that tourist-visa holders may not work, including voluntary work. Overstaying costs US$30 per day and you cannot leave until it is paid (FCDO). An older Belgium-embassy page (2020 procedures) listed a 90-day single-entry option (US$70), but a 2024 trade article says 90-day e-visas were withdrawn and FCDO mentions only the 30-day option, so max_stay_days is 30 and the 90-day option is unconfirmed. Passport: FCDO says valid at least 6 months after arrival; Global Affairs Canada says at least 6 months beyond your planned departure from Ethiopia and that it must be stamped on arrival; follow the stricter rule. Yellow fever: a certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with yellow fever transmission risk, which includes airport layovers longer than 12 hours there (CDC, reviewed 25 Aug 2026; FCDO says the same without the 12-hour detail); Global Affairs Canada names Brazil, Bolivia, Peru and Venezuela (arriving from or transiting an airport in them). Travellers coming directly from a non-risk country do not need one. Exemptions in FCDO's list are only for holders of an Ethiopian diplomatic ID card, temporary residence permit or Ethiopian Origin ID (Yellow Card); this passport is not exempt. Catch: an old Ethiopian-embassy page (Belgium, 2018) says e-visa holders must enter through Addis Ababa Bole airport and lists eligible countries (the list differs from a 2020 page); check both on evisa.gov.et. Security: both FCDO and Global Affairs Canada advise against travel to large parts of the country, including all of Amhara; read them before booking.
fee_notes: Fee amount not confirmed from a readable official page: evisa.gov.et renders client-side and returned no text to my fetcher, FCDO and Global Affairs Canada give no amounts, and Ethiopian embassy pages conflict (Washington embassy page, undated: single-entry tourist visa US$60 by money order; Belgium embassy e-visa page, written for 2020 procedures: US$50 for up to 30 days plus a US$2 online processing fee). Third-party guides report US$62 for 30 days but I could not open an official page showing it, so the portal's fee table before payment is the authority. Fees are not refundable (Belgium embassy page).

conditions_text: India is on the Department of Immigration's list of 51 nationalities that must get a visa before travelling to Zambia: 'Applicants must apply for the visa through the Director General of Immigration prior to their arrival into Zambia', online through the eServices portal (eservices.zambiaimmigration.gov.zm), and obtain an approval letter before departing. Indian passport holders do not appear on the visa-exempt list or the visa-on-arrival list, so do not count on getting a visa at the airport. e-Visa holders must show the approval letter and payment receipt at entry and can use any port of entry. Documents listed for a tourism visa: passport-sized photo, passport copy, signed cover letter addressed to the Director-General, hotel booking and a copy of the return air ticket (jpg, png or tiff). Processing time is not stated on the pages checked. Validity of the visa is the window to enter, not the length of stay; the length of stay granted is not stated for this category on the pages checked, so max_stay_days is left empty. Passport: at least six months' validity from entry and at least three blank pages (Immigration visitor page). Yellow fever certificate if arriving from a transmission-risk country (FCDO).
fee_notes: Single entry US$50 statutory fee (US$50.50 with card admin fee), double entry US$80 (US$80.80), multiple entry US$80 (US$80.80), day tripper US$10 (US$10.10), per the Department's fee page (no effective date stated; a 2026 increase is reported by secondary sites). KAZA UNIVISA eligibility is limited to a nationality list; India was not seen in the examples given, so do not assume it.

conditions_text: Brazil is on the Department of Immigration's list of nationals who can obtain a visa on arrival at any port of entry, from selected Zambian missions abroad, or online through the eServices portal. Brazil is not on the visa-exempt list. Catches: air arrivals must hold a valid return air ticket and land or water arrivals must show enough funds; on-arrival applicants need full details and a physical address of their host or lodging for the whole stay. Passport: at least six months' validity from entry and at least three blank pages (Immigration visitor page). The visa's validity is the window to enter, not the period you may remain, and the length of stay granted is not stated for this category on the pages checked, so max_stay_days is left empty. A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a transmission-risk country (FCDO) and Brazil has transmission-risk areas, so check the certificate requirement before travel. Applying online ahead of travel avoids queues at the airport.
fee_notes: Single entry US$50 statutory fee (US$50.50 with card admin fee), double entry US$80 (US$80.80), multiple entry US$80 (US$80.80), day tripper US$10 (US$10.10), per the Department's fee page (no effective date stated). The fee on arrival is not separately listed, so confirm payment methods at the border.

conditions_text: Zimbabwe's official e-visa site (evisa.gov.zw FAQ) lists this passport among the countries whose holders need a visa but do not have to get it in advance: they pay for and obtain the visa on entry. Visa on arrival is valid one month from issue; you can instead apply online beforehand through evisa.gov.zw (single entry, one month; double entry, three months; multiple entry, six months). The e-visa FAQ says average processing is seven working days and advises applying at least 3 weeks before travel; with visa on arrival nothing is applied for in advance, and the FAQ says the entry declaration can be pre-filled online. The FAQ states validity (one month for single entry) but not a separate 'maximum stay' figure, so 30 days is taken from validity; the UK FCDO says visas on arrival are 'usually valid for 30 days' and Global Affairs Canada says a single-entry visa is valid for 30 days with two consecutive extensions possible at a Department of Immigration office, up to 90 days in total. Catch: pay in US dollars cash, in small notes (UK FCDO). The KAZA UniVisa (Zimbabwe plus Zambia, with day trips into Botswana) is also sold: US$50 for 30 days per the UK FCDO, available at Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls airports and the Victoria Falls and Kazungula land borders; the FCDO describes it as covering travel between Zimbabwe and Zambia and day trips into Botswana only. Yellow fever certificate is required only if arriving from a country with yellow fever transmission risk (FCDO, Global Affairs Canada). Declare cash or travellers cheques of US$10,000 or more; the FCDO says leaving with more than US$2,000 in cash is illegal. Passport: the Zimbabwean embassy in Washington lists a passport valid for at least 6 months; the UK FCDO says it must expire at least 6 months after arrival and have 3 blank pages; Global Affairs Canada says 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave and at least 2 blank pages. Follow the strictest: 6 months beyond departure and 3 blank pages. Indian passport holders are not exempt and are not in the 'visa required before travel' list on the e-visa FAQ.
fee_notes: Official general schedule (Zimbabwean embassy in Washington and Paris pages, port-of-entry fees, 'subject to change'): US$30 single entry, US$45 double entry, US$55 multiple entry (multiple entry needs a supporting letter). Double-entry visa on arrival lasts three months; multiple-entry visa on arrival (six months) is available only to UK, USA and Canada passport holders per evisa.gov.zw. The e-visa site shows the exact amount in the approval response and fees are not refunded if refused. KAZA UniVisa US$50 (UK FCDO). Some tour-company sites report higher nationality-specific fees for UK/Irish and Canadian passports, but no official page opened states them, so they are not given here; confirm the amount for your passport on evisa.gov.zw before paying.

Passport: the Zimbabwean embassy in Washington lists a passport valid for at least 6 months, and the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada both say 6 months' validity with 2 to 3 blank pages for their own travellers, so carry 6 months beyond departure and 3 blank pages to be safe. Yellow fever certificate only if arriving from a country with transmission risk. Declare cash or travellers cheques of US$10,000 or more.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-exempt nationals per evisa.gov.zw FAQ ('Entry without Visa': free pre-arrival declaration). Park, activity and other fees are separate.

conditions_text: A visa is required for tourism and it is issued online as a tourist eVisa through Madagascar's official portal (evisamada-mg.com; the portal says evisamada.gov.mg is the only official application site and warns about pirate sites). It is in force today, all nationalities are eligible, and the portal says it can be applied for between one week and six months before departure; the authorisation is issued within 72 hours of a validated application and must be shown (printed or on a phone) at arrival. The same visa can also be bought on arrival at the eVisa counters, and the portal says online prices equal arrival prices. Stay: the portal describes the eVisa as single-entry with a maximum stay of 60 days; its fee table runs to 90 days (tiers 0-15, 16-30, 31-60 and 61-90 days), and a visa can be extended at the Immigration office up to 90 days in total (portal FAQ; FCDO and Global Affairs Canada also cap a total stay at 90 days). Catch: FCDO and Global Affairs Canada describe stays of up to 15 days as visa-free (FCDO: with an administration fee and onward ticket) with a visa for longer stays, but Madagascar's own portal now lists a fee for 0-15 days, so budget for the fee rather than relying on a 15-day exemption.  Source note: the portal says all nationalities are eligible; no India-specific page was found, and no visa cascade for held documents was found. Passport: FCDO and Global Affairs Canada both say valid at least 6 months after arrival with 2 blank pages (the portal says only 'currently valid', so follow the stricter rule); carry a return or onward ticket. Health: FCDO lists Ebola entry restrictions (travellers who were in or transited an affected country in the last 21 days may be refused entry unless exempt, plus a health declaration and screening on arrival) with no end date; yellow fever proof only if arriving from a country with yellow fever risk.
fee_notes: Official fee table on the portal, in force from 16 February 2026: 0-15 days EUR 30 / USD 35; 16-30 days EUR 35 / USD 41; 31-60 days EUR 40 / USD 47; 61-90 days EUR 50 / USD 59. Visa extension: 210,000 MGA. Payment by Visa or MasterCard on the portal. Diplomats and employees of certain organisations are exempt from the fee. Embassy-issued visas and the on-arrival payment methods (FCDO: USD, EUR or ariary cash) were not confirmed on a Madagascar government page.

conditions_text: Uganda requires an online e-visa for this passport, in force today, and issues no visas on arrival (Uganda Citizenship and Immigration Control notice). Apply on the official portal visas.immigration.go.ug before travel and carry the approval letter. The single-entry tourist visa can be granted for up to 3 months (90 days); the approval is valid for 90 days from the approval date, after which it lapses and you must reapply, and the initial stay can be extended by 60 days in two intervals (immigration.go.ug tourist-visa page). Documents listed for tourism: passport copy with at least 6 months' validity remaining, a tour plan, itinerary or booking, a recent photo, and a hotel booking or address. Regional option: the East African Tourist Visa (USD 100, 90 days, multiple entries into Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda only, issued only for tourism, not renewable, and the issuing country must be your first point of entry). Yellow fever: Uganda's immigration directorate posted a notice dated 2 October 2026 that a yellow fever vaccination certificate is no longer mandatory for entry, and UK FCDO removed the requirement from its page on 8 October 2026; the older CDC page (April 2025) still says proof is required for travellers aged 1 and over, so if you hold a certificate carry it, and WHO/CDC still recommend the vaccine for Uganda. India is not on Uganda's visa-exempt list (checked on the immigration.go.ug visa-exempt page).
fee_notes: Single-entry tourist visa USD 50, non-refundable, plus a bank charge on the payment (immigration.go.ug tourist-visa page). East African Tourist Visa USD 100 (immigration.go.ug East African Tourist Visa page). Multiple-entry and other fee tiers are in the 2021 fees notice and are not needed for a tourist trip.

fee_notes: Single-entry tourist visa USD 50, non-refundable, plus a bank charge on the payment (immigration.go.ug tourist-visa page). East African Tourist Visa USD 100 (immigration.go.ug East African Tourist Visa page). Multiple-entry and other fee tiers are in the 2021 fees notice and are not needed for a tourist trip.

conditions_text: Singapore is on the visa-exempt list published by Uganda's immigration directorate (Uganda 'DO NOT REQUIRE VISA'). The page does not state a maximum stay for exempt nationals, so max_stay_days is left empty; confirm the permitted stay with Uganda's immigration directorate or your airline. A 2021 notice from the same directorate says exempt nationals still need a passport valid at least 6 months, and (per that notice) an invitation or conference letter and a yellow fever certificate at the point of entry; the current visa-exempt page does not repeat the invitation requirement, so carry onward/return tickets, accommodation details and a passport valid at least 6 months beyond your stay. Yellow fever: a 2 October 2026 directorate notice says the certificate is no longer mandatory, but WHO/CDC still recommend vaccination for Uganda. Uganda issues no visas on arrival, so a Singapore passport holder staying for an unusual purpose (work, study, volunteering) should check the correct permit first.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-exempt nationals (immigration.go.ug visa-exempt page lists no fee). The East African Tourist Visa (USD 100) is not needed for Uganda-only travel.

conditions_text: India is in Category B ('Visa Consular') on the Guatemalan immigration institute's (IGM) country classification, so an Indian passport holder needs a Guatemalan tourist visa issued by a Guatemalan embassy or consulate before travel. Acuerdo IGM-015-2025 art. 10 asks for the visa form, a valid passport, a travel itinerary, income proof or bank statements for the last three months (Spanish or English), and an international credit card (a debit card needs three months of statements as well); an interview may be required. Art. 14: a tourist stay is at most 90 days, extendable once for an equal period, never beyond 180 days from entry. Exception: a Category B national who holds a valid US, Mexican, Canadian or Schengen visa is exempt from the consular visa and treated as Category A (see the held-document rules). Sources do not say whether the held visa must be multiple-entry or how much validity it needs, nor whether a transit visa counts; the regulation just says 'visa vigente' (valid visa). Whether Guatemala has a mission accessible to Indian applicants was not confirmed from an official page; ask a Guatemalan consulate.
fee_notes: Consular visa fees are in IGM's tariff (Acuerdo IGM-029-2023 as reformed by IGM-039-2025); the amount was not read from the tariff, so check with the consulate.

conditions_text: Indian passport holders are Category B (consular visa) in Guatemala, but art. 10 of Acuerdo IGM-015-2025 exempts Category B nationals who hold a valid visa of the United States, Mexico, Canada or a Schengen state from the consular visa; they are treated as Category A (visa exempt). This rule models a valid USA visa as the held document. The regulation says only 'visa vigente' and does not state minimum validity, entry type or whether a transit visa counts. Once treated as Category A the tourist stay is up to 90 days (art. 14 for visa-based stays: extendable once for an equal period, never beyond 180 days from entry), counted across the CA-4 countries. Carry the visa and passport (UK FCDO and Germany's Auswaertiges Amt advise 6 months' passport validity on arrival; Canada says 6 months beyond departure), and complete the online traveller declaration before entering and leaving (per FCDO, GAC and Auswaertiges Amt). The entry decision stays with the immigration officer.
fee_notes: No Guatemalan visa fee for the exempted traveller; a US$30 departure tax is normally included in the air ticket (FCDO).

conditions_text: Guatemala's immigration institute (IGM) lists this nationality in Category A, 'Exento de visa' (visa exempt). Under the CA-4 arrangement the stay is counted from first entry into Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras or Nicaragua and is shared across them; crossing between them does not restart it. US citizens need no visa for tourism. The stay is set by the immigration officer at first entry and is generally 90 days (UK, Canadian and German government advice for their own nationals gives 90 days; Canada notes Guatemala allows up to 180 at the officer's discretion, extendable at the IGM before expiry). Passport: governments advising on Guatemala (UK, Canada, Germany) give 6 months' validity; confirm for US passports. The US State Department page was blocked to automated fetching (HTTP 403), so the classification comes from IGM and the stay figure from the other governments' pages. Complete the online traveller declaration before arrival and departure and get an entry stamp.
fee_notes: US$30 airport departure tax, normally included in the ticket (FCDO). Officials may ask for illegal 'entry fees' at land borders; none is due for visa-exempt nationals (FCDO).

conditions_text: UK nationals can visit Guatemala for up to 90 days without a visa (UK FCDO). The 90 days start at first entry into Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras or Nicaragua and do not restart when you cross between them; British nationals need a visa for Honduras. A 30-day extension can be requested before the 90 days expire (FCDO). Overstaying means a fine paid before leaving. Passport must be valid 6 months after arrival with at least 2 blank pages. Complete the online immigration declaration form before entering and exiting; get your passport stamped on entry. Children aged 17 and under travelling alone or with one parent need a notarised letter in Spanish. FCDO's page does not mention an onward-ticket requirement.
fee_notes: US$30 airport departure tax (or the same in quetzales), normally included in the ticket. Overstay fine payable before departure.

conditions_text: Canadians do not need a visa for tourist or business stays of up to 90 days (Global Affairs Canada, updated 13 October 2026). Under the CA-4 agreement they move freely among El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua; the officer at first entry sets the length of stay and Guatemala allows a maximum of 180 days; extensions must be requested at the IGM before the authorised stay expires. After leaving the CA-4 region you must wait 72 hours before returning, and re-entry can still be refused. Passport valid at least 6 months beyond planned departure (airlines may be stricter). Complete the electronic declaration before arriving and departing and keep the QR code; an entry stamp is required and a missing one can cause fines at departure. Minors travelling with one parent or a third party need a notarised consent letter.
fee_notes: No visa fee. US$30 departure tax normally included in the air ticket (per UK FCDO).

conditions_text: Indian ordinary-passport holders need a Uruguayan visa issued before travel. Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior visa-regime table (page dated 19/08/2025) lists India as 'Necesita Visa (5)' for a common passport, with footnote (5) reading 'Necesita autorizacion previa' (prior authorisation required); diplomatic and service passports do not need a visa. The Foreign Ministry says the application is made in person at the Uruguayan consulate covering your place of residence (the online form is for enquiries only, there is no online application on that page), the consul interviews you and forwards the file to the Direccion Nacional de Migracion (DNM), and approval usually takes at least 20 working days. Documents listed: application form, invitation letter or hotel booking plus proof of funds, passport valid at least 6 months after arrival, one passport photo and a travel reservation. After approval you have 60 days to have the visa issued in the passport and a further 60 days to enter Uruguay. The catch: no concession is documented for Indians holding a valid US, Schengen or UK visa or residence permit; the only visa-holder concessions in the table are for Dominican (US or UK visa) and Chinese (US, Canadian, UK or EU visa) passports, so do not assume a US or Schengen visa lets you in. The permitted length of stay is set by the visa; the pages opened do not state it, so max_stay_days is left null.
fee_notes: Consular fee 3 'pesos consulares' (stated as US$42), charged only if the visa is granted; consular fees are reset every 1 January (Foreign Ministry page last updated 21/10/2020, so confirm the current amount with the consulate).

conditions_text: No visa needed for tourism. Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior visa-regime table (page dated 19/08/2025) lists this passport as 'No necesita Visa' for a common (ordinary) passport. Diplomatic and service passports are treated differently and are not covered here. US citizens may stay up to 90 days as a tourist (the table's footnote (6) names 90 days as the established term for visa-free entry; the US State Department page could not be opened, so the stay length rests on the Uruguayan table). A passport valid at entry with a blank page for the stamp is the safe standard; no onward-ticket rule appears on the Uruguayan pages opened. Non-tourist purposes (work, or staying longer) require prior consultation with Migration.

British citizens can visit Uruguay without a visa for up to 90 days (FCDO). Your passport must be valid for the whole stay and have at least one blank page for an entry stamp. FCDO's page does not mention an onward or return ticket. To stay longer or take up residency contact the Direccion Nacional de Migracion. Uruguay's own visa table (19/08/2025) also lists Gran Bretana as 'No necesita Visa' for a common passport. Children aged 17 or under travelling alone or with one parent may need a 'Permiso de Menor' (written permission) from the absent parent.

Global Affairs Canada: no tourist visa is needed for stays of up to 90 days, and the same 90-day limit applies for business travel. To stay longer you must ask the migration authorities for an extension once you are in the country. Your passport must be valid for the expected duration of your stay (airlines may enforce stricter rules). A student visa is required for study. Uruguay's visa table (19/08/2025) also lists Canada as 'No necesita Visa' for a common passport, while diplomatic and service passports need a visa. GAC does not mention an onward-ticket requirement.

No visa needed for tourism. Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior visa-regime table (page dated 19/08/2025) lists this passport as 'No necesita Visa' for a common (ordinary) passport. Diplomatic and service passports are treated differently and are not covered here. Australian citizens may stay up to 90 days as a tourist (the table's footnote (6) names 90 days as the established term; the Smartraveller page timed out when opened, so the stay length rests on the Uruguayan table). Non-tourist purposes (work, or staying longer) require prior consultation with Migration. No onward-ticket rule appears on the Uruguayan pages opened.

German tourists with a valid passport do not need an entry visa for stays of up to 90 days (Auswaertiges Amt). The catch: only a passport is accepted. The Foreign Office lists Reisepass, vorlaeufiger Reisepass and Kinderreisepass as accepted and Personalausweis (ID card) and vorlaeufiger Personalausweis as not accepted; documents must be valid on entry and the page states no minimum remaining validity. One extension can be requested from the Uruguayan immigration authority shortly before the 90 days expire; a further extension requires a temporary residence permit. EU freedom of movement does not apply in Uruguay. Uruguay's visa table (19/08/2025) also lists Alemania as 'No necesita Visa'.

No visa needed for tourism. Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior visa-regime table (page dated 19/08/2025) lists this passport as 'No necesita Visa' for a common (ordinary) passport. Diplomatic and service passports are treated differently and are not covered here. Singapore citizens may stay up to 90 days as a tourist (the table's footnote (6) names 90 days as the established term for visa-free entry; no Singapore government page was opened, so the stay length rests on the Uruguayan table). Non-tourist purposes (work, or staying longer) require prior consultation with Migration. No onward-ticket or validity figure for Singapore passports appears on the Uruguayan pages opened; carry a passport valid for the stay.

No visa needed. Uruguay's visa table (19/08/2025) lists Brasil as 'No necesita Visa', and Brazil's consulate in Montevideo says Brazilian tourists can stay up to 90 days, extendable by another 90 (Mercosur partner). Accepted documents per the Brazilian consulate (page last updated 04/12/2023): a passport valid at least 6 months, or a valid RG (state-issued identity card); the page warns an old or worn RG may be refused by Uruguayan immigration. A driver's licence (CNH) and professional cards (OAB, CREA etc.) are not accepted. Foreign residents of Brazil can use a valid CRNM. Overstaying is fined.

India is on the Fiji Ministry of Immigration's list of visa-exempt countries, so no visa is needed before travel for a visit. Visitors from visa-exempt countries are given a visitor permit on arrival at Immigration Clearance, valid for up to 4 months (the Ministry of Immigration says up to, so the officer sets the actual period), and it can be extended by up to 2 more months if you apply and pay before the first permit expires. Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says to carry a valid passport (its FAQ says valid for more than 6 months from the date of travel), a return or onward ticket (a one-way ticket is not accepted), a confirmed address in Fiji and proof of sufficient funds; the Visit/Transit page also lists 'requisite fees ($F96)' for visitors at clearance, so ask your airline or the Ministry whether that applies to you. Every arriving traveller must hand in a completed and signed Arrival Card (the Immigration page does not say whether an online version is available, so fill the paper card the airline gives you or check with the Ministry). A visitor permit does not allow work or study, and the officer makes the final entry decision. Travellers who are only transiting Fiji to another country within 72 hours of entry need a transit visa arranged before arrival, per the Ministry; this is not the tourist case.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Ministry's Visit/Transit page lists 'requisite fees ($F96)' to present at Immigration Clearance for visitors other than medical-treatment and yacht/crew arrivals, but does not say exactly what the fee covers; extension fee not stated on the Ministry pages checked.
